locale_scope: Guam official orthography; CNMI differences require separate review
rights: Original English exercise prompts; sources linked for reference only; no media or source text copied
help_policy: Give instructions or an unrelated worked example only; do not reveal independent answers.

lessons.title: Meet the writing system
lessons.objective: Recognize that CHamoru has a documented spelling system and that pronunciation needs a separate listening lesson.

practice.prompt: Find the word in this lesson that names the CHamoru spelling system: orthography, calendar, or recipe.
In your own words, explain why spelling rules and pronunciation recordings are different kinds of evidence.
With the choices hidden, name the type of reference you would check before changing a written CHamoru word.

lessons.title: Six written vowel symbols
lessons.objective: Recognize the written vowel symbols a, å, e, i, o, u without guessing how they sound.

practice.prompt: Find the vowel with a ring above it in this group: a, å, e.
From a, å, e, i, o, u, sort the two a-shaped symbols separately.
Without looking at the examples, write all six vowel symbols used in the referenced spelling description.

lessons.title: CH is one letter
lessons.objective: Understand that CH represents one letter in the referenced official alphabet.

practice.prompt: When reading the official alphabet, should CH be treated as one letter or two? Explain what source you checked.
Compare the letter count of CH with the two visible characters used to write it.
After hiding the explanation, describe how CH is treated in the referenced spelling system.

lessons.title: Syllables and spelling variation
lessons.objective: Distinguish syllable-aware spelling study from claims of correct pronunciation, and recognize that Guam and CNMI conventions can differ.

practice.prompt: Why might a beginner need to study syllable boundaries before attempting to read a longer word?
Two references spell the same word differently. Name one responsible check before labeling either spelling wrong.
Without hints, state two things a fluent reviewer should verify before this lesson becomes graded.
